ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526/1999 (creation of UIAF and financial information regime), Law 1121/2006 (money laundering and financing of terrorism countermeasures), Law 2010/2019 (final beneficial owner reporting mandate), Decree 830/2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUB), Decree 1674/2016 (AML/CFT risk management framework), and Articles 105 to 112 of the Colombian Commercial Code (Código de Comercio).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the country of incorporation of the foreign shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the foreign shareholder's domicile

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Colombian registered agent / incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or corporate body of the foreign shareholder or ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille + Consular Legalization if not a Hague Convention jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of the passport and UBO/PEP self-certification for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of residence of the beneficial owner

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official Spanish translation of all foreign documents, prepared by a certified translator registered with the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator / Ministry of Foreign Affairs authorized translation registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Apostille applied to the underlying document

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and ultimate beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Colombia's UIAF state lists, and the Colombian Superintendency of Companies list of persons linked to money laundering. PEP status must be self-declared and independently verified using commercial data sources. Enhanced due diligence applies to any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, cash-intensive activity, or politically sensitive corporate structure. Rescreening must occur at least quarterly and upon any material change in control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social) via the local Cámara de Comercio, including the Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali as applicable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be filed in Spanish using the Spanish alphabet. Names originating in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters and accompanied by an official Spanish translation. The registered name must be distinctive, must not be confusingly similar to existing trademarks or trade names, and must end with the abbreviation 'S.A.S.' when used as the corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice issued by the Cámara de Comercio, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' before the same Chamber within ten (10) business days of notification. If the Chamber confirms the rejection, the applicant may file a 'recurso de apelación' before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within five (5) business days. A rejected name cannot be reserved again under the same wording; a fresh name application must be filed after the administrative appeal is exhausted or the appeal window lapses.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-office service address is accepted for incorporation purposes and for receiving official correspondence. However, the company must maintain a physical establishment in Colombia where books and records are available for inspection, and the corporate secretarial activity being licensed requires sufficient physical infrastructure and staff presence to evidence commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% to 30% risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection in the first twelve months, depending on the volume of foreign-client relationships and the assessed medium-risk AML/CFT profile of registered-agent activity.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under Decree 1074/2015 and chamber fee schedule

stage_2.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA); local environmental authority: Secretaría Distrital de Ambiente (Bogotá) or Corporación Autónoma Regional (C.A.R.) of the location
stage_2.classification_tier: Exempt — Category IV (administrative/professional services): this activity is not listed among projects requiring environmental license under Decree 1076/2015 and Resolution 1409/2018. The office activity discharges no significant industrial effluents or atmospheric emissions; an optional 'Concepto Ambiental' / environmental health clearance from the municipal environmental authority may be requested for the principal office.
stage_2.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: domestic discharges to municipal sewerage must stay within Resolution 0631/2015 maximum permissible parameters (pH 6.0–9.0; BOD5, COD, total suspended solids and fats/oils limits as set out in Annex 1); discharges outside public sewer systems require a concession from the C.A.R. Atmospheric: emergency generators, if installed, below the emission threshold requiring an atmospheric discharge permit under Resolution 909/2008 (monitor and log maintenance); VOC/fugitive emissions from office printing and consumables remain negligible but any future solvent printers/stationary sources must comply with Resolution 909/2008 PELs. Waste handling: comply with color-coded segregation under Resolution 2184/2019, special waste rules for batteries/e-waste (Resolution 0485/2020... actually 0485 of 2020? There is a Resolution 0485 of 2020 on PCB? no. For e-waste, Resolution 1512 of 2010/0979? For batteries, Resolution 0371 of 2009. I'd say

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (Colombian National Tax and Customs Directorate); official digital portal: www.dian.gov.co (tax, customs, and electronic-invoicing platform MUISCA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign parent or shareholder: preregister with DIAN through the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) digital procedure using Form 002, selecting foreign non-resident entity status; DIAN assigns a NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) upon presentation of constituting documents and power of attorney. For the Colombian S.A.S.: execute the private incorporation document without minimum capital, file the pre-RUT through the Chamber of Commerce one-stop digital portal, receive the provisional NIT, complete mercantile registration, and then obtain the definitive corporate NIT and update the RUT to include VAT responsible status (IVA Régimen Común) and the exporter-of-services status. The procedure additionally requires a Colombian legal representative, a digital signature certificate, and activation of the electronic-invoicing accreditation before issuing sales invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Colombian S.A.S. is a resident corporation for Colombian income tax purposes, subject to tax on worldwide income at the 35% corporate rate for tax year 2024; Colombia does not allow pass-through or flow-through taxation for a S.A.S. For indirect-tax purposes, the entity is a VAT responsible party (Régimen Común) once engaged in taxable supplies; services that meet the Article 481 numeral 3 E.T. export criteria are excluded from IVA with entitlement to credit/refund, and the RUT responsibility tag must evidence exporter-of-services status to support the 0% rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Relevant statutory mechanisms for a services S.A.S. include: (i) the optional Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLES), an integrated turnover-based election available where annual gross income falls below the statutory UVT ceiling of Article 906 E.T. (approximately COP 3.7-4.7 billion for 2024 depending on activity), which consolidates income tax, VAT, industry and commerce tax, and wealth-tax surcharges; (ii) advance-pricing agreements and unilateral transfer-pricing elections; (iii) treaty-benefit attestation and beneficial-ownership declarations for the applicable double-taxation treaty; and (iv) hybrid-mismatch and disregarded-entity disclosure obligations under Law 2277 of 2022, requiring proof of the counterparty tax character before claiming deductions or credits in cross-border secretarial-fee structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - IVA (Impuesto sobre las Ventas), a national consumption tax levied under Articles 420-481 of the Estatuto Tributario, complemented by the national consumption tax on certain specified services; no subnational sales tax applies in the unitary jurisdiction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no monetary threshold for VAT liability in Colombia: any person, individual or entity, that sells taxable goods or renders taxable services in the national territory is a VAT responsible party and must register in the RUT. The simplified VAT contributor regime (Régimen Simplificado del IVA) is restricted to natural persons with prior-year gross income under approximately 3,500 UVT (about COP 164.7 million for 2024), and is unavailable to a corporate S.A.S.; the SIMPLES optional regime ceiling (about 80,000-100,000 UVT) is not a VAT exemption but an elective consolidated-tax switch with its own eligibility requirements for service activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (factura electrónica de venta, FEV) is mandatory for all VAT responsible parties under DIAN Resolution 000012 of 2021 and Resolution 000165 of 2023. Invoices must be generated in XML (UBL or CII), digitally signed with a qualified electronic signature, transmitted in real time to DIAN through the pre-validation API, and delivered to the client only after DIAN returns the unique electronic invoice code (CUFE) and validation status. The issuer may use an authorised technology provider or DIAN free solution; batch reporting must occur within 10 calendar days; contingency procedures are allowed only for justified technological failure; XML records and CUFE validation histories must be archived for at least 5 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Services supplied from Colombia to foreign recipients qualify for the 0% VAT rate and refundable input credits under Article 481 numeral 3 of the Estatuto Tributario where: (i) the beneficiary is a person or entity without Colombian residence, domicile, or permanent establishment; (ii) the services are executed and utilised exclusively abroad; (iii) the benefit is not derived from Colombian-source activities, goods located in Colombia, or Colombian assets; and (iv) the consideration is received in foreign currency through the official foreign-exchange market (Mercado Cambiario) within the legally prescribed settlement term. Registered-agent, corporate-secretarial, and offshore directorship services rendered to a non-resident client generally meet the exclusive-foreign-use test; however, any local physical performance by Colombian-based staff, local board meetings in Colombia, or services connected with Colombian assets will recharacterise the income as Colombian-source and render the supply taxable at 19%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Formulario No. 50 - Declaración de Exportación de Servicios (service export declaration) accepted electronically by DIAN through VUCE
CUFE-dated electronic invoice (FEV) issued at 0% with the statutory export annotation
International service contract or commercial proposal identifying the non-resident beneficiary, scope of registered-office and secretarial services, place of use and benefit abroad, and consideration
Exporter-of-services status certificate or a certification from the foreign client confirming exclusive use and economic benefit outside Colombia
Declaración de Cambio (foreign-exchange settlement form) issued by an authorised Colombian bank or foreign-exchange intermediary evidencing conversion of the export proceeds
SWIFT MT103 bank wire credit advice evidencing receipt of the foreign currency in the Colombian account of the S.A.S.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN cross-references the service-export declaration, electronic invoices, RUT status, beneficiary documentation, and foreign-exchange records (CIS and Mercado Cambiario databases). Failure to repatriate and settle the proceeds through the official exchange market within 180 days destroys the zero-rating claim, making the IVA due at 19% plus daily interest and triggering the inaccurate-return penalty of up to 200% of the tax difference under Article 648 E.T., in addition to the information-filing penalty of Article 651 E.T. Retrospective audits may reopen returns and reverse input credits or refunds for the full five-year statute of limitations; fictitious or fraudulent export documentation additionally subjects the company and legal representative to criminal tax-fraud prosecution under Law 2277 of 2022, with imprisonment for significant evasion, disqualification from public contracts, and reputational blacklisting. Transfer-pricing records and arm's-length documentation for intra-group secretarial fees must also be maintained, as DIAN may otherwise reclassify the receipt as Colombian-source royalty or service income with a 35% corporate tax assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (BanRep), acting through its Junta Directiva, jointly with the Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público for foreign-exchange and foreign-investment policy; operational oversight and enforcement carried out by the Subdirección de Control Cambiario of BanRep and the Comité de Inversiones Extranjeras.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is the sole legal tender. Under Law 9 of 1991 and Resolution 8 of 2000, current-account transactions are freely convertible, while capital-account operations are freely admissible but require mandatory registration with BanRep. Dividend remittance and capital repatriation are lawful once the underlying foreign investment is registered with BanRep and the corresponding exchange declaration is channeled through an authorized intermediary of the foreign-exchange market. Practical hurdles: (i) all cross-border receipts and payments for export or import of services must be channeled through an IMC; (ii) export invoice proceeds must be repatriated within the statutory collection term; (iii) profit repatriation requires evidence of tax payment in Colombia, including the certificado de retención and the corresponding DIAN proof; and (iv) receipts parked in unregistered offshore fiduciary or EMI accounts may be treated as an exchange-control violation unless subsequently channeled in time to an IMC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Colombia does not impose a forced conversion ratio of export proceeds into COP; however, a mandatory full-channeling obligation applies under the Régimen Cambiario. 100% of the commercial value of exported services, including registered-agent and offshore secretarial fees billed to foreign clients, must enter Colombia and be routed through an IMC. The statutory collection term is six months counted from the date the service is rendered. Channeling is evidenced by the Declaración de Cambio por Exportación de Servicios, supported by the commercial invoice and, where applicable, the certificado de prestación de servicios al exterior. Uncollected export receivables must be reported and corrected; late channeling is subject to fines imposed under the exchange-control sanction regime. Once repatriated, the funds may either be converted freely through the spot exchange market or maintained in foreign-currency accounts, but any subsequent conversion must still occur through an IMC.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account — Cuenta Corriente Empresarial (COP) with USD-facing treasury desk and SWIFT access
Operational Account — Cuenta Corriente/Cuenta de Ahorros Empresarial with international banking desk
Operational Account — Cuenta Corriente Empresarial with digital onboarding and FX module
Operational Account — Cuenta Corriente Empresarial with global connectivity
Operational Account — Corporate Account with cross-border banking overlay

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, dLocal, Mercury-type platforms) may be used only as a complementary collection or disbursement tool, not as the primary clearing rail. Legal constraints: (1) offshore EMIs are not Intermediarios del Mercado Cambiario and therefore cannot receive export proceeds on a Colombian resident's behalf without triggering the channeling obligation and the six-month repatriation deadline; (2) the Superintendencia Financiera AML/SARLAFT framework expects Colombian banks to verify that the S.A.S. does not use offshore virtual accounts to evade exchange control; (3) most EMIs decline to onboard Colombian regulated-service S.A.S. entities because of the medium-risk rating and the presence of non-resident UBOs; and (4) if used, the account must be limited to a capped monthly flow, with monthly reconciliation against IMC channelings and BanRep declarations. The recommended cap is below 20% of monthly collections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes — a physical or high-assurance video-verified interview is mandatory for the legal representative, UBOs and principal signatories. Fully remote account opening without any Colombian contact is not available for a non-resident-managed S.A.S. In practice, the legal representative or a locally appointed apoderado must attend an in-person interview before activation; post-Covid supervisory criteria permit reliable video-identification where the representative is outside Colombia, but this is accepted only alongside apostilled powers of attorney, Cámara de Comercio excerpts, NIT certification, and reduced transaction limits until post-verification is completed. Tier-1 banks require the UBO structure, source-of-funds explanation and an economic-substance narrative for the Colombian service platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company-formation and registered-agent activities for clients incorporated in high-risk or opaque jurisdictions are treated as a shell-company and potential money-transmission red flag, leading to compliance-committee rejection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled engagement letters for each foreign client; economic-purpose narrative per client; UBO registry of the S.A.S.; adverse-media screening report; formal AML/CFT SARLAFT manual of the S.A.S.; corporate group chart; signed statutory declaration that bearer shares do not exist under Law 1258/2008 and that the S.A.S. never transits client funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound SWIFT credits from multiple unrelated third parties without matching underlying service invoices, interpreted as possible fund clearing or layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chronological invoice register and signed service agreements; export-service attestation filed at the Cámara de Comercio; monthly service-export status report reconciling each payment with the corresponding declaración de cambio; source-of-funds letters from remitters; independent third-party accountant certification; and appointment of an internal compliance officer who performs ongoing transaction monitoring.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident legal representative or UBO resident in a zero-tax or offshore jurisdiction triggers enhanced due diligence and may be refused without an evidentiary local anchor.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport copies; police clearance from the jurisdiction of residence; tax-residence certificates; beneficial-ownership chain chart; sworn source-of-wealth statement; proof of a leased Colombian office and payroll; DIAN peace-and-sanction certificate; and the Cámara de Comercio registration of a locally domiciled executive director or apoderado with full banking authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Representation of foreign companies that are struck-off, under investigation, or named on sanctions and watchlists, creating reputational and legal contamination risks for the bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening of every appointing company against OFAC, UN, FATF and EU sanctions lists; sub-delegation of the appointing-agent function under a compliance-conditioned service agreement; confirmation that each appointing company is active in its home registry; legal opinion from local counsel in the client's jurisdiction confirming capacity; and the bank's watchlist exit memorandum.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant sequence is: (i) incorporate the S.A.S. and obtain the NIT from DIAN; (ii) open a COP current account with an IMC such as Bancolombia; (iii) receive a SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's own corporate account, stating the beneficiary as the S.A.S. with its NIT and the purpose concept 'Aporte de capital — Inversión directa en Colombia, actividad ISIC 8299'; (iv) instruct the IMC to channel the incoming foreign currency on receipt and to present the Declaración de Cambio por Inversión Internacional, together with the FDI registration (Registro de Inversión Extranjera), within the five business days following channeling; (v) preserve the accepted BanRep exchange declaration as the legal basis for future dividend remittance and capital repatriation; (vi) record the contribution in the S.A.S. books and file any capital-increase document with the Cámara de Comercio; and (vii) for amounts above USD 50,000, retain the cross-referenced MT103 UETR, the exchange-declaration sequential code and board minutes to satisfy DIAN and Control Cambiario audits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound payments covering subcontractor fees, software-as-a-service, licensing, and international vendor costs, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103/gpi through the local IMC bank. Service imports must be paid via the exchange market by submitting the Declaración de Cambio por Importación de Servicios at the moment of payment. Colombian law requires the payor to withhold applicable income tax (typically 10-20% for foreign service fees, subject to treaty relief) and to remit the withholding to DIAN using the corresponding electronic form. Commercial letters of credit under UCP600 are generally not appropriate for secretarial or registered-agent service flows and are reserved for merchandise or high-value physical deliveries. For recurring outflows, banks offer virtual-treasury batch payment portals with pre-registered beneficiaries; every disbursement must be paired with the underlying invoice, contract and evidence of economic substance to prevent exchange-control or tax-credit rejection.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/COP deliverable currency forwards (forwards a medida) contracted with an authorized local IMC, subject to an underlying commercial exposure such as future service-export collections or planned foreign-investment transactions.

USD/COP cross-currency swaps executed with a local IMC for converting registered foreign-debt obligations or planned capital expenditures from COP to USD, supported by underlying exposure and BanRep-instrument registration.
European-style USD/COP FX options (call or put) purchased from a local IMC to hedge collection uncertainty and protect the S.A.S. balance sheet without creating asymmetric speculative risk.

Offshore COP non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only where a local IMC provides a matched back-to-back synthetic hedge; direct offshore NDFs without the participation of an IMC are not authorized for Colombian resident treasury operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil — annual renewal of the commercial registration of the SAS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered-office jurisdiction (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each year for companies with a 31 December fiscal year; no grace period for same-year renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers Cámara de Comercio fines and late-payment surcharges, a non-renewed status in the public registry, loss of legal standing to contract unless cured, and eventual administrative cancellation of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Estados Financieros + Informe de Gestión + Informe del Revisor Fiscal — statutory deposit of annual financial statements and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered-office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve financial statements by 31 March following fiscal year-end; deposit in Cámara de Comercio is due within one month after approval, normally in April for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit blocks the annual mercantile renewal and exposes administrators and the company to fines of up to 17 SMMLV; persistent default creates an adverse registry status and supports administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios) with all applicable annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Legal-entity taxpayers must file by the August deadline published by DIAN for the relevant tax year using the last two digits of the NIT; for calendar-year companies this is generally between August and early September of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty of 5% of tax due per month or fraction, capped at 100% of tax due, with a minimum of 1,000 UVT; interest runs on unpaid tax, and DIAN may embargo bank accounts and suspend the taxpayer's RUT status after formal collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) — annual beneficial-ownership confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June immediately following each tax year-end; must reflect the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners as of 31 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, late filing, or false information is penalized under Colombian Tax Code provisions for RUB noncompliance, with fines up to 1,000 UVT per infraction and certificates of compliance (paz y salvo) may be withheld for public-contracting and registration purposes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A legal statutory audit is mandatory for a SAS when, at year-end, gross total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (2025: COP 7,117,500,000) or gross annual income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (2025: COP 4,270,500,000). The Revisor Fiscal requirement may also be imposed by the bylaws or because the company performs regulated public-interest activities; once the threshold is met, appointment of a Revisor Fiscal is obligatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian financial statements must be prepared under Decree 2420/2015 and subsequent amendments, which adopt the IASB IFRS framework: NIIF Plenas for Grupo 1, NIIF para las PYMES for Grupo 2, and micro-entity standards for Grupo 3. Statements are presented in Colombian pesos (COP) and Spanish.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For every share transfer, ownership is effective against the company only after inscription in the share register; the annual RUB filing must confirm the ultimate natural-person beneficial owner, any person holding more than 5% interest or voting rights, and any person exercising control. Changes during the year must be reflected in an updated RUB within the time set by DIAN, and all ownership records must be reconciled with the Cámara de Comercio data before issuance of the annual compliance certificate.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas/Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea General de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–650 per year for registered-agent, secretarial, and office-service support in major Colombian cities; Cámara de Comercio tariffs and notarial/protocol costs are billed separately and vary with company assets.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200–4,000 per year for a small or medium SAS subject to statutory review; fees rise with asset complexity, number of subsidiaries, and the scope of the Revisor Fiscal's opinion.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory holiday for ISIC 8299 corporate secretarial services. Preferential deductions are limited to Article 235-2 of the Tax Code (R&D, renewable energy, water and tourism investments); none apply to registered-agent or offshore secretarial revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 220 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios de Entidades) filed electronically through DIAN's Ventanilla Virtual and the Sedes de Impuestos Nacionales portal (www.dian.gov.co).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (Yearly); quarterly self-advance payments (anticipos) are also required for the subsequent fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the annual return must be filed no later than the DIAN filing-calendar date established by resolution based on the last two digits of the NIT, generally between March 10 and May 29 of the year following the taxable year. Non-calendar-year entities may be assigned a special deadline by DIAN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Razón Social: exact commercial name of the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada as registered in the Cámara de Comercio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Transliterate the legal name into Latin script and ensure it exactly matches the registration certificate of the Colombian entity or branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIT: Número de Identificación Tributaria assigned by DIAN.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident cannot file the return without first obtaining an NIT through its registered agent; this field is mandatory and must match the DIAN data base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actividad CIIU: International Standard Industrial Classification code for the primary commercial activity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 8299 (Business Support Services / Corporate Secretarial). Secondary activities must be listed in annexes; incorrect codes can trigger audit queries.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ingresos Brutos: total gross income accrued or received during the fiscal year, net of returns, discounts and cancellations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the offshore secretarial company, include all worldwide income only if the entity is resident; non-resident entities include only income effectively connected with a Colombian permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gastos Operacionales: deductible operating expenses (salaries, rent, professional service fees, insurance, software licences).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses corresponding to the generation of taxable Colombian income are deductible; intercompany costs must be at arm's length and supported by valid invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Renta Líquida: net taxable income after deductible expenses, exempt income and excluded costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply transfer pricing adjustments, thin-capitalisation rules and any treaty-protected income definitions in the computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Impuesto de Renta: corporate income tax at 35% of the taxable base after tax credits and advance prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The statutory rate applies to the Colombian SAS as a resident entity; no additional sectorial surcharge applies to ISIC 8299.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Descuentos Tributarios: credits for double-taxation relief, compensation of previous balances and VAT on fixed assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign investors may claim treaty relief only after obtaining the applicable beneficial-owner declaration and prior-year documentation; otherwise the credit is disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Saldo a Favor: final balance after prepayments, withholdings and credits; negative amounts are tax credits to be offset or refunded.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not claim this credit on their personal returns; the credit remains with the Colombian entity and can be used in subsequent annual filings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of the tax due per month (or fraction) up to a maximum of 100% of the tax due; if no tax is due, the penalty is between 0.5% of gross income and 10 UVT, whichever is higher. Filing with inaccurate or false data triggers a penalty of 1% to 20% of the understated or omitted amount, plus daily arrears interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 7.5% on dividends distributed from profits already subject to the 35% corporate tax; 35% on dividends paid out of exempt or specially-taxed corporate profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced rate under a Double Tax Agreement (e.g., US-Colombia or UK-Colombia), the foreign investor must (a) provide a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority; (b) submit the completed Form EXC-4 and a heat-and-email authorisation through DIAN's online system; (c) obtain a DIAN acceptance of the beneficial-owner declaration; (d) file the corresponding tax-return annexure evidencing a real economic presence and not mailbox status; and (e) instruct the Colombian SAS to withhold at the reduced treaty rate only after the DIAN process is approved. The DTA does not apply automatically; the payor must retain the entire withholding unless the protocol is completed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic interest withholding: 15% for qualifying financial loans (reducible to 10% under the US-Colombia treaty for banking institutions). Cross-border royalties for patents, software licences and proprietary know-how: statutory 15% domestic rate (reducible to 10% for qualified treaty partners; certain films and TV royalties at 5% under US treaty protocols). Non-financial technical service fees are treated as royalties and thus subject to 15%; general other-income payments to a non-resident are subject to the 33% residual rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is required when the taxpayer's gross income exceeds COP 6,335,662,000, or gross assets exceed COP 6,335,662,000, or yearly related-party payments exceed COP 1,935,000,000 (all thresholds indexed by UVT for tax year 2024; approximately USD 1.5 million gross income/assets and USD 450,000 related payments). Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required for multinational groups with consolidated revenues greater than EUR 750 million or an equivalent local amount.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the general anti-avoidance rule (Article 869-2 of the Tax Code) and substance-over-form doctrine require a SAS providing offshore secretarial services to have real premises, at least one direct local employee with managerial capacity, and active supervision of registered agents. The absence of such substance triggers the disallowance of deductions, reclassification of management fees as dividends, and application of CFC and thin-cap rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting gross service fees, issuing fictitious supplier invoices for non-existent secretarial sub-agents, or understating taxable income to zero through artificial deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of 48 to 108 months under Article 434A of the Criminal Code, Law 1762/2015. Administrative penalty under Article 647 of the Tax Code of 1% to 20% of understated tax, plus arrears interest of two times the official rate; asset seizure and suspension of the NIT if payment is not regularised.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, auditors and registered agents who knowingly signed fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax. Courts order travel bans, civil restitution of the misappropriated amounts, automatic removal from the Cámara de Comercio registry, and a 10-year ban from public contracting. Private criminal liability results in disqualification from acting as a corporate officer.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exceeding the Local File threshold and failing to file the annual Informe de Precios de Transferencia, or executing intercompany secretarial management-fee contracts with no actual delivery of services, employees or personnel in Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may adjust taxable income by the difference between the arm's length price and the invoiced price. A penalty of 5% of the related-party transaction value is imposed for non-filing of the TP informativo (Art. 651 E.T.); on adjustment, an additional 20% surcharge applies to the extra tax assessed. Failure to produce the Master File or Local File after request yields an additional fine of 10% of the asset value relating to the controlled transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as 'tax managers' are personally liable for the adjusted tax and penalties when documents prove wilful negligence. Colombian courts pierce the corporate veil under Article 60 of the SL Code when the SAS functions as a letterbox; the management of the non-resident parent may then be named as joint debtor and their assets in Colombia embargoed. Persistent non-compliance may trigger criminal charges for attempted tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a nominee registered agent for non-resident shell vehicles that move proceeds from third-country tax evasion, the sale of smuggled goods, or corrupt payments into the Colombian financial system while maintaining no real commercial purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: UIAF administrative fine of up to 200,000 current monthly minimum legal wages (approx. COP 260 billion), revocation of the professional licence, and asset seizure under Law 526/1999. Criminal charge under Article 323 of the Criminal Code ('Lavado de activos') carries imprisonment of 9 to 15 years and a fine of 500 to 1,000 current legal monthly minimum wages; the corporate business is compulsorily wound up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing is routinely applied in AML cases: shareholders, directors and representative agents who knowingly sponsor shell companies are jointly and severally liable for all civil compensation and the full administrative fine. Travel bans, indefinite disqualification from serving as corporate officers, and confiscation of all fees collected in the shell operation are judicially ordered in final convictions; directors may be extradited under mutual legal assistance treaties.
